questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wished to go somewhere where English was the first language as it makes for an easier transition and makes socializing with new people and cultures more accessible

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough, the university sent everything by email beforehand and everything else could be found on their website

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest but doable. I just kept an eye on different housing groups for students in Boulder on Facebook and wrote the ones that fit my needs. My best advise is to start super early because most people post available rooms a semester in advance

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Is the best option in Boulder if you aren't 19. It gives you more freedom and having a roommate makes it easier to make more friends while you're there. It is quite expensive in Boulder so be prepared to pay around 6000-9000 a month for rent.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Review the course catalouge on the website (remember to check that you are looking at the right semester as different courses are available in spring and fall). Put the courses you want in the shopping cart and click apply. Super simple. Just make sure the courses have enough credit hours for your needs and that they dont overlap.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I just wrote an email to whoever was listed as head of a specific department if I had any questions regarding a course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got both of the ones I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose something you find interesting and something you can't get at KU

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did both first and second year grad courses but the academic level in general was a bit lower than we are used to in Denmark, so don't be afraid to pick them over under-grad courses. After talking with the other Danish exchange students who did under-grad, I discovered that I had significantly less classes, coursework and tests than them. Do grad-level courses if you are taking a Masters, it's less work than under-grad courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They encourage more open discussion in classes than just a professor lecturing for an hour

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Food Systems
Communication for Sustainable Impact

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Deffinatly the communications class. Very useful even tho I haven't had any previous classes in communication.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The excessive tipping that is expected when you go out

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and rent is extremely expensive. Fresh and healthy food especially. Take advantage of the University's free food pantry.
Public transportation in Boulder and Denver is free with your student card and so is the Uni's fitness and Rec center.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many different options and the school offer a bunch of free activities if you are interested. There is something for everybody.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Everything that offers free food

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around. Rent a car. Take the bus to Rocky Mountain National Park. You are smack in the middel of US and can visit some fun places by taking a 2 hour trip by plane.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, but it is always a bit special to move to another part of the world

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the activities hosted by the university

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most things are significantly less accessible if you don't have car

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are super friendly and really want to help and include you. Take all the help you can get. If they offer to drive you around, say yes. You are not a burden to them because they are used to helping and taking care of their friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make friends, both exchange and local
Travel outside of Boulder
Embrace the American social culture even if it feels a bit overexcited and weird to you. It makes it more fun to be around Americans

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Uni rents out bikes for 50 usd per semester. Much easier than trying to buy one and then having to sell it again after a semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends. Especially the other Danes there on exchange as I still have the opportunity to see them regularly when I'm back in Copenhagen

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritizing traveling as it feels very expensive, but it is worth it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
